appraisal_events.evidence: « — Dumont ! Oh ! je me méfie. » ; puis, après « quelques questions plus précises » posées « adroitement » et un « interrogatoire dissimulé » qui force l’invité « à confesser ses origines », le grand-père fredonne « De ce timide Israélite / Quoi, vous guidez ici les pas ! »
appraisal_events.explanation: The grandfather turns the naming of a friend into a covert test of Jewish origin and then announces his verdict to the family in coded operatic quotation, marking the named guest as a suspect outsider. The narrator stages this as a practiced family game, reporting the mockery with amused distance rather than subscribing to its judgment.

status_effects.explanation: He gains local rhetorical command: he extracts the confession unnoticed (« à son insu »), keeps his verdict in allusive song, and holds the family as a knowing audience that reads his signals.

Named only to be distrusted, he is locally recategorized as a suspected intruder in the household — the quoted line about a « timide Israélite » being guided into a place not his own makes the exclusion explicit.

ambiguities: The narrator's stance toward the grandfather's detection ritual is genuinely underdetermined: the comic relish of the reporting (« adroitement », « imperceptiblement ») can be read as fond appreciation of his cleverness or as quiet exposure of his ethnic suspicion, and the choice governs whether the grandfather is locally elevated as a wit or diminished as a bigot.

Reference resolution of the coded song's target: Dumont is named only in the dialogue and is absent from the reference sheet, while the second half shifts to a generic « patient lui-même déjà arrivé », so it is unclear whether the final hum aims at Dumont or at an unnamed guest of the same class of suspects.
